trust_decision.summary: Before unescaping a static-file wildcard, reject any value that still contains a percent-encoded path separator (%2F/%2f/%5C/%5c) as 404, and normalise fs.FS names with path.Clean rather than filepath.Clean; decided in echo.StaticDirectoryHandler and in the group branch of middleware/static.go's Static middleware.

landing_point.why: The summary says an encoded slash 'exposes static files'; the first thing an engineer greps is the static handler, and echo.go:592 is the only url.PathUnescape on the echoed wildcard in the root package.

fix_sites.entry_point: echo.Static / echo.StaticFS / Group.Static / Group.StaticFS / StaticDirectoryHandler (direct public API)
fix_sites.module_kind: root echo package, static file handler

fix_sites.entry_point: same handler chain (filepath.Clean -> path.Clean for fs.FS names)
middleware.Static / middleware.StaticWithConfig / StaticConfig.ToMiddleware, when mounted on a group wildcard (`c.Path()` ends in `*`)
fix_sites.module_kind: middleware package, second static file server

fix_sites.entry_point: none (new shared helper HasEncodedPathSeparator, called from both handlers)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver can argue the Static middleware is a separate, opt-in `e.Use` feature and that the report and the fix comment are about echo.StaticFS/StaticDirectoryHandler unescaping, so the middleware's own unescape branch (and its `e.Use` branch that reads already-decoded URL.Path) is 'a different feature, not this advisory'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Files whose on-disk names literally contain a percent sign must still be downloadable from an already-decoded URL.Path (and percent-encoded ../ traversal must stay blocked); an over-broad fix that rejects any '%', or that unescapes URL.Path a second time, breaks these legitimate cases. The double-encoded %252F case must also keep resolving to a literal filename, not a separator.

O6_input_shapes: %5C / %5c encoded backslash (Windows separator, neutralised by path.Clean)
%252F double-encoded: must unescape once to a literal filename, not a separator
raw still-encoded wildcard param (c.Param("*")) vs already-decoded URL.Path (two different value sources)

O7_producer.where: router.go:796-803 (matches on URL.RawPath) and router.go:1025-1033 (optional UnescapePathParamValues)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: middleware.Static / StaticWithConfig mounted with e.Use (no wildcard route): the branch reads the already-decoded c.Request().URL.Path, so pathUnescape is false and the new HasEncodedPathSeparator check never runs; /admin%2Fsecret.txt misses the protected /admin/* route, reaches the 404 chain where the global chain still runs, and the middleware opens admin/secret.txt from the root
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: URL.Path is already decoded by net/http on this branch, so there is 'no unescaping bug to fix here'; the documented root-level usage has no route-level static path and auth is 'the application's job'.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the fixed site, different branch; 0 packages

O8_uncovered_routes.route: RouterConfig{UnescapePathParamValues: true} (public via echo.Config.Router): router.go:1028 decodes the wildcard before any handler/middleware sees it, so HasEncodedPathSeparator(c.Param("*")) sees '/' and passes and a static route still resolves across the boundary; likewise StaticDirectoryHandler(fs, true) skips the new check entirely
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Opt-in, non-default router configuration (and the fix's own comment scopes the protection to the default raw-path router), so 'enabling param unescaping is the application's explicit choice'.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: root package, router layer, 1 package from middleware; the check sits in handlers, not in the router

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a canonical-path/directory redirect that rebuilds Location from c.Request().URL.Path instead of the cleaned fs name
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This branch already exists for the trailing-slash redirect and is exactly the code behind the pre-existing 'open redirect vulnerability' test case, so a maintainer touching redirects would edit here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a StaticConfig.Index / directory-browse path that re-joins user-influenced segments (path.Join(filePath, config.Index)) without the separator check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Index and Browse are configurable features of this middleware; a maintainer adding an index override or listing would reuse filePath here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a FileFS/StaticFileHandler variant that takes the on-disk name from a route param (e.g. 'serve file named by :name') and cleans/joins it itself
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: fsFile is the shared low-level opener for c.File/FileFS and the static handler; a maintainer adding a param-driven file route would go through it directly and bypass both checks.

O9_family: path traversal via encoded path separator / route-matching bypass (CWE-22, A01)
